label: Accolade
summary: The accolade a game text is about, handed to the text by the game.
details: Vanilla's accolade texts use it to name the accolade (`[ACCOLADE.GetName]`) and its primary type, for example in the confirmation that an accolade gains a new attribute.

label: Active council task
summary: The council task a game text is about, the one a councillor is carrying out.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts and messages: to name the task or its type ("finishes ... task"), and to reach the councillor doing it, as in "Fire ... from the council". COUNCIL_TASK gives the same kind of object.

label: Activity
summary: The activity (a special occasion hosted for a purpose, such as a hunt) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name the activity a character is sent to ("You will go to ..."); it appears in about 40 lines.

label: Activity intent
summary: The activity intent (what a character personally seeks to accomplish at an activity) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to name the intent in condition texts ("must have the ... intent") and in the activity window's warning that an intent has no valid target.

label: Activity option
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to one option chosen for an activity.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Activity option category
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to a category that groups activity options.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Activity phase
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to one phase of an activity.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Special guest role
summary: The special guest role of an activity a game text is about, such as a role someone must attend in.
details: Vanilla's activity planner warnings use it to name the role ("Someone must attend as the ...", "... has died and can no longer attend as the ..."), mostly through its name as the host sees it.

label: Activity type
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to an activity type.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Actor
summary: The character who acts in what a game text describes, for example the one who starts an interaction.
details: Vanilla pairs it with RECIPIENT, the other side: "[ACTOR] married [RECIPIENT]" in house relation reasons, and the greeting line of an interaction notification, picked by the actor towards the target character.

label: Agent slot
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to an agent slot (a place for a spy or agent in a scheme).
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: AI watch windows on
summary: Going by its name, whether the AI watch windows (debug windows about the AI) are switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of a part of the cardinals window; one more use in the character window is commented out. It returns true or false.

label: Army
summary: A named reference to an army, used at the start of a chain such as `ARMY.GetName`.
details: Vanilla uses it in the military view texts to print the army's name.

label: Army regiment
summary: One regiment entry of an army that a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's army view lists it as name and strength: the regiment's name, then its current count over its maximum ("[name]: [count]/[max]").

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 120 lines, for example to say an artifact is destroyed or to show its durability (current over maximum) when that changes.

label: Attacker
summary: A named reference to the character who attacks, in texts about a war.
details: Vanilla uses the word only as a text key name in the war results window; the line shown does not show it used as an object, so this rests on the name and return type (a character).

label: Abandon ruler objective
summary: Going by its name, a GUI command that abandons the player's ruler objective.
details: Vanilla passes it to `CreateCommandPopup` on a click and to `GetCommandDesc` for the tooltip. Its return type is Command.

label: Absolute value (decimal)
summary: The value of a decimal number without its minus sign.
details: It takes one decimal number. Vanilla uses it once, on a value in a vassal contract text (interactions_l_english.yml:1367).

fields.name: value
fields.text: The number to make positive.

label: Absolute value (float)
summary: Going by its name, the value of a floating-point number without its minus sign.
details: It takes one number. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The number to make positive.

label: Absolute value (whole number)
summary: The value of a whole number without its minus sign.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a court grandeur difference and a scheme agent's contribution as positive numbers.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The whole number to make positive.

label: Council window
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the council window of the interface.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Court window
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the court window of the interface.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Game rules
summary: Gives access to the game rules (the settings chosen for a game).
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the game rules screen and of the ruler designer window.

label: Knights view
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the knights view of the interface.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source in the accolade creation window, written `CreateAccoladeView.AccessKnightsView`.

label: Local player data
summary: Going by its name, gives access to cached data of the local player (the player at this computer).
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source of the main HUD. Its return type is not registered, so the game gives no more detail.

label: Log viewer
summary: Gives access to the central log viewer.
details: The game's own description is "Access Central Log Viewer". Vanilla never uses it.

label: Map editor layer borders
summary: Gives access to all layer borders in the map editor.
details: This is a tool for the map editor. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Message feed
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the handler of the message feed (the stream of notifications).
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: My realm window
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the My Realm window of the interface.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Suggestion items
summary: Going by its name, gives access to suggestion entries of the interface.
details: Its return type is not registered, the game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses it.

label: Top bar
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the top bar of the interface.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data source in the activity locale window and the royal court window. Its return type is not registered.

label: Activity type has cooldown
summary: Whether the activity type has a cooldown for the player, meaning its cooldown is more than 0 days.
details: The game defines it as the type's cooldown in days for the player being greater than zero. Vanilla uses it in the activity list window text about what hosting gives.

fields.name: type
fields.text: The activity type to check.

label: Add line
summary: Going by its name, adds the given text on a new line.
details: Vanilla puts it right after a heading to append an extra description, such as what completing a legend does. Whether it skips empty text is not documented. It returns text.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The text to put on a new line.

label: Add text key if
summary: Adds the text of a localization key when a condition is true.
details: Vanilla writes it as `AddLocalizationIf( Character.IsRuler, 'AI_ECONOMIC_ARCHETYPE_TT' )` in the AI personality tooltip, so the first argument is the condition and the second the key in quotes. It returns text.

fields.name: condition
fields.text: Whether to add the text.

fields.name: key
fields.text: The localization key whose text is added.

label: Add paragraph
summary: Going by its name, adds the given text as a new paragraph.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla appends the holy site effect description under a tooltip heading. It returns text.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The text to add.

label: Add text if
summary: Adds the given text when a condition is true.
details: Vanilla uses it in tooltips, for example to add a hint line only when nothing has been changed yet. The first argument is the condition, the second the text. It returns text.

fields.name: condition
fields.text: Whether to add the text.

fields.name: text
fields.text: The text to add.

label: Add watch window
summary: Going by its name, opens a watch window for the given object.
details: Vanilla calls it on click with an activity, a character or a confederation (made with `MakeScope`) as the argument. It returns nothing.

fields.name: object
fields.text: The thing to watch.

label: Add decimals
summary: The sum of two decimal numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tribute mission texts to add two gold values from variables.

fields.name: first
fields.text: The first number.

fields.name: second
fields.text: The second number.

label: Add 2D vectors
summary: Going by its name, the sum of two two-part vectors (x and y).
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Add 3D vectors
summary: Going by its name, the sum of two three-part vectors (x, y and z).
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Add 4D vectors
summary: Going by its name, the sum of two four-part vectors.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Add floats
summary: Going by its name, the sum of two floating-point numbers.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Add whole numbers
summary: The sum of two whole numbers.
details: Vanilla uses it in the commission artifact decision texts, for example to add the artifacts owned in two slot types.

fields.name: first
fields.text: The first number.

fields.name: second
fields.text: The second number.

label: Add unsigned numbers
summary: Going by its name, the sum of two whole numbers that cannot be negative.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: And
summary: Whether both of its two arguments are true.
details: It is used a great deal in GUI conditions and texts. For more than two conditions, nest it or use `And3` to `And8`.

fields.name: first
fields.text: The first condition.

fields.name: second
fields.text: The second condition.

label: And (2 conditions)
summary: Whether both of its two arguments are true.
details: It does the same as `And`. Vanilla never uses this name.

label: And (3 conditions)
summary: Whether all three arguments are true.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI visibility conditions, for example on the HUD.

label: And (4 conditions)
summary: Whether all four arguments are true.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI visibility conditions, for example in the declare war window.

label: And (5 conditions)
summary: Whether all five arguments are true.
details: Vanilla uses it in GUI visibility conditions, for example in the title window.

label: And (6 conditions)
summary: Whether all six arguments are true.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: And (7 conditions)
summary: Whether all seven arguments are true.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: And (8 conditions)
summary: Whether all eight arguments are true.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Application
summary: Going by its name and return type, gives access to the game application itself.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Achievements available
summary: Whether achievements can be used in this game session.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla uses it to enable a button in the main menu. It returns true or false.

label: Bookmark character
summary: A character offered on a start-date bookmark, as the bookmark screen describes them.
details: Vanilla's bookmark texts use it to show the character's primary title (tier and name) and culture.

label: Building
summary: A named reference to a building, used in texts about constructing or having one.
details: Vanilla writes it as `$BUILDING|V$` in holding texts to print the building's name, for example "Constructing ...".

label: Bind fold-out
summary: Adds a fold-out (collapsible section) data context to a widget.
details: Vanilla calls it when a widget is created. It returns nothing.

label: Bind tabs
summary: Adds a tabs data context to a widget.
details: Vanilla calls it when a widget is created. It returns nothing.

label: True/false to frame
summary: Going by its name, turns a true/false value into 1 or 2 (1 for false, 2 for true).
details: Vanilla uses it as the `frame` of icons, for example for an expanded state or a shown category. It returns a whole number.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The true/false value.

label: True/false to frame (reversed)
summary: Going by its name, turns a true/false value into 2 or 1 (2 for false, 1 for true).
details: Vanilla uses it as the `frame` of icons, for example for sort direction or a top-displayed state. It returns a whole number.

fields.name: value
fields.text: The true/false value.

label: Byte to text
summary: Going by its name, turns a byte value into text.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Character
summary: A named reference to a character, used at the start of a chain such as `CHARACTER.GetShortUIName`.
details: Vanilla uses it very often in effect and interaction texts, where the game fills in the character the text is about.

label: Character memory
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to a memory a character holds.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Date checked
summary: The date a condition text compares against.
details: Vanilla's epidemic condition texts use it to show the date an outbreak's start is compared with ("Began before ..."), written out as text.

label: Claimant
summary: The character whose claim a war is fought for, in war texts.
details: Vanilla's war names use it: "War for [claimant]'s Claim on the ..." and the claim casus belli's name.

label: Confederation
summary: The confederation a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's confederation texts use it to name the confederation, for example in the condition text "Is a member of ...".

label: Confederation type
summary: The type of confederation a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in the names of confederation cohesion modifiers, such as "Leading ..." or "Aligned to ..." followed by a level.

label: Council position
summary: The council position (a seat on a ruler's council) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in condition texts ("Has the Council position ...") and in the warning that someone appointed to it cannot be fired or moved.

label: Council task
summary: The council task a game text is about, carried out by a councillor.
details: Vanilla's council texts use it for the councillor's position name and the current task's type, for example the warning that the current task will be aborted when a new one is given. It gives the same kind of object as ACTIVE_COUNCIL_TASK.

label: Council task type
summary: The kind of council task a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to name the task when sending a councillor: "Send your [position] to [task] on [county]".

label: County
summary: The county a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the county a councillor is sent to work on, naming it through its title (`[COUNTY.GetTitle.GetName]`).

label: Court position
summary: A named reference to a court position, used in texts about it.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip text about revoking a court position.

label: Court position task type
summary: Going by its name and return type, a named reference to a task type of a court position.
details: The game documents nothing more, and vanilla never uses this name.

label: Court position
summary: The court position a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name the position someone is appointed to ("You will appoint ... as your ...").

label: Culture
summary: A named reference to a culture, written `$CULTURE.GetName$` in texts.
details: Vanilla uses it in culture trigger texts, for example "... culture has not discovered ...".

label: Culture pillar
summary: The culture pillar (one of the basic building blocks of a culture, such as its language) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it, for example, to name the language a character learns ("learns the ... language").

label: Culture tradition
summary: The culture tradition a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to name a tradition a culture gains or loses.

label: Rite divergence percent
summary: The divergence of a faith rite as a percentage.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla passes a rite (`Rite.Self`) in the faith view and prints the result with a `%0` format. It returns a decimal number.

fields.name: rite
fields.text: The rite to measure.

label: Rite divergence score
summary: The divergence score of a faith rite.
details: Vanilla uses it in the faith view next to the "rite divergence" label for a given rite. It returns a decimal number.

fields.name: rite
fields.text: The rite to measure.

label: Progress between dates
summary: Gives the percentage of how far the current date is between a start date and an end date.
details: It takes three arguments; the game's documentation names only the start and end date and does not say what the third is. It returns a float. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Resolution aspect limit
summary: A two-part size limited by the screen's aspect ratio.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla uses it as the `size` of a part of the royal court window. It returns a two-part vector (width and height).

label: Breakdown items
summary: Going by its name, builds the lines of a breakdown for the given object.
details: Vanilla passes an army (`Army.Self`) as the data model of a tooltip. Its return type is not registered.

fields.name: object
fields.text: The thing to break down.

label: Calculate script value
summary: Calculates the named script value with the target character as its root.
details: Vanilla uses it in the AI debug window to show values such as the AI's minimum men-at-arms spending, formatted with `|V2`.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the value is calculated for.

fields.name: script value
fields.text: The name of the script value.
fields.values: a script value name in quotes

label: Anyone can unpause
summary: Whether any player is able to unpause the game.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla combines it with `IsPausedByMe` to decide what the pause button shows. It returns true or false.

label: Can change map mode
summary: Going by its name, whether the map mode can be changed.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the map mode selector in the map editor and in the visibility of the map modes bar. It returns true or false.

label: Can slow down
summary: Going by its name, whether the game speed can be lowered.
details: It returns true or false. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Can show locale view
summary: True when no activity event is open and the activity locale view is set to the given view.
details: Vanilla passes view names such as 'phase_information' or 'my_knights_window' to decide which tournament panel shows.

fields.name: view
fields.text: The name of the locale view.

label: Can edit settings after host
summary: Whether the settings can still be edited after hosting a multiplayer game.
details: The game notes that this depends on the multiplayer platform. Vanilla uses it to enable and show parts of the multiplayer screen.

label: Can get achievements
summary: Whether achievements can be earned in this game.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla shows one part of the in-game menu when it is true and another when it is false. It returns true or false.

label: Can speed up
summary: Going by its name, whether the game speed can be raised.
details: It returns true or false. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Can make landless character
summary: Whether a landless character can be made.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the multiplayer screen. It returns true or false.

label: Can make noble family characters
summary: Whether noble family characters can be made.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla uses it for the visibility of a part of the multiplayer screen. It returns true or false.

label: Can open lobby
summary: Going by its name, whether a multiplayer lobby can be opened.
details: Vanilla combines it with checks for an open lobby, ironman and multiplayer to decide which pause menu button shows. It returns true or false.

label: Can compete in martial contest
summary: Whether the player can compete in the martial contests hosted by the given host.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tournament texts that explain why the player cannot compete. The tooltip function `CanPlayerCompeteInMartialContestTooltip` gives the reasons.

fields.name: host
fields.text: The host of the contests.

label: Martial contest tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for `CanPlayerCompeteInMartialContest`.
details: Vanilla uses it next to that function in the "You cannot compete in this contest" texts.

fields.name: host
fields.text: The host of the contests.

label: Can see activity log entry
summary: Whether the player may see this activity log entry.
details: The game's macro makes an entry visible unless it has the tag `crime`; a crime entry is visible only when its character is the player. The game's documentation text talks about intent entries instead, which does not match the macro. Vanilla uses it as the visibility of entries in the activity locale window.

label: Can raze holdings
summary: Whether the character's government allows razing holdings.
details: The game defines it as the character's government having the government flag `can_raze_holdings`. Vanilla passes the player and combines it with checks that the player holds the title and has not leased it out, to show a raze button.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character who would raze.

label: Can tick day
summary: Going by its name, whether the game can advance by a day.
details: It returns true or false. Vanilla never uses it.

label: You are / she is
summary: Gives the word "are" when the text is about the player, and "is" when it is about someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it a lot in texts so one line reads right for both, for example "X is a member of a confederation".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You become / she becomes
summary: Gives "become" for the local player and "becomes" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "X becomes a vassal of Y".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You consider / she considers
summary: Gives "consider" for the local player and "considers" for someone else.
details: Vanilla has one use, in a clerical text; the line shown does not itself show the call, so this rests on the game's documentation and the name.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You control / she controls
summary: Gives "control" for the local player and "controls" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about counties a character controls.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You create / she creates
summary: Gives "create" for the local player and "creates" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text about founding a new kingdom.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You do / she does
summary: Gives "do" for the local player and "does" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "X does not have any vassals ...".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You don't / she doesn't
summary: Gives "don't" for the local player and "doesn't" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in interaction texts and nickname descriptions.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You fancy / she fancies
summary: Gives "fancy" for the local player and "fancies" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in a nickname description.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You follow / she follows
summary: Gives "follow" for the local player and "follows" for someone else.
details: Vanilla has one use, in the cardinals window text; the line shown is cut off before the call.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You gain / she gains
summary: Gives "gain" for the local player and "gains" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in a clerical text about gaining spiritual fulfillment.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You go / she goes
summary: Gives "go" for the local player and "goes" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in nickname descriptions such as "Wherever she goes ...".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You have / she has
summary: Gives "have" for the local player and "has" for someone else.
details: The game's own description reads "I You have / SheHe has", which looks like a typo. Vanilla uses it often, for example in "X already has a strong hook on Y".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You hold / she holds
summary: Gives "hold" for the local player and "holds" for someone else.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You join / she joins
summary: Gives "join" for the local player and "joins" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in ecumenical council texts about joining the innovators or the conservatives.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You lease / she leases
summary: Gives "lease" for the local player and "leases" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text about leasing a title out to a holy order.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You lose / she loses
summary: Gives "lose" for the local player and "loses" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in a clerical text about losing spiritual fulfillment.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Me / her or him
summary: Gives "me" for the local player and "her" or "him" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in a Japan decision text, for example "will prepare him ...".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: My / first name's
summary: Gives "my" for the local player and the character's possessive first name for someone else.
details: The game's example is "My / Geoff's"; the macro itself writes lowercase, and vanilla capitalises with `|U`. Vanilla uses it in a Japan decision text and a great project text.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: My / her or his
summary: Gives "my" for the local player and "her" or "his" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "My thing / HerHis thing", the word only, the thing is written after it. The one vanilla line shown is cut off before the call, so how it is used there is not visible.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You oppose / she opposes
summary: Gives "oppose" for the local player and "opposes" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about an investor opposing a candidate.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You start / she starts
summary: Gives "start" for the local player and "starts" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text about starting a war.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You support / she supports
summary: Gives "support" for the local player and "supports" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts about an investor supporting a candidate.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You switch / she switches
summary: Gives "switch" for the local player and "switches" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in ecumenical council texts about changing stance.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You try / she tries
summary: Gives "try" for the local player and "tries" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in a nickname description.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You were / she was
summary: Gives "were" for the local player and "was" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in nickname descriptions about the past.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You win / she wins
summary: Gives "win" for the local player and "wins" for someone else.
details: Vanilla uses it in titles of a tenet-spreading activity.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You / first name
summary: Gives "you" for the local player and the character's first name for someone else.
details: The game's example is "You / Geoff". Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You / her or him
summary: Gives "you" for the local player and "her" or "him" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Everyone calls you the XYZ / Everyone calls HerHim the XYZ".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You / she or he
summary: Gives "you" for the local player and "she" or "he" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "You are / SheHe is". Vanilla uses it very often (199 uses), for example in nickname and interaction texts.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You / them
summary: Gives "you" for the local player and "them" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Has only brought you closer / Has only brought them closer".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: You / they
summary: Gives "you" for the local player and "they" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "And you have / And they have".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Your / first name's
summary: Gives "your" for the local player and the character's possessive first name for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Your / Geoff's". Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Yourself / herself or himself
summary: Gives "yourself" for the local player and "herself" or "himself" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "About yourself / About HerHimself".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Your / her or his
summary: Gives "your" for the local player and "her" or "his" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Your thing / HerHis thing"; the thing itself is written after it. It is used very often in effect, faction and nickname texts.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Your / their
summary: Gives "your" for the local player and "their" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Your mutual interests have / Their mutual interests have".

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Yours / her or his
summary: Gives "yours" for the local player and "her" or "his" for someone else.
details: The game's example is "Thing is yours / Thing is HerHis". Vanilla uses it in nickname and interaction texts.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character the text is about.

label: Has progress to victory
summary: Whether the character has progress to victory.
details: The game defines it as the character's PtV value being greater than 0. "PtV" is read as progress to victory from the game's documentation. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Clear admin vassal candidate
summary: Clears the vassal candidate shown in the details of the government administration window.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on click in that window. It returns nothing.

label: Clear contest tab
summary: Clears the contest tab of the activity locale view.
details: The game defines it as clearing the variable `activity_contest_info_tab`. Vanilla calls it when the tournament contest information panel starts.

label: Clear error log
summary: Clears the error log.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on a right click in a shared component. It returns nothing.

label: Clear explored faiths
summary: Going by its name, clears the list of faiths marked as explored.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on click in the HUD and the map mode controls. It returns nothing.

label: Clear explored houses
summary: Going by its name, clears the list of houses marked as explored.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on click in the HUD and the map mode controls. It returns nothing.

label: Clear explored realms
summary: Going by its name, clears the list of realms marked as explored.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on click in the HUD and the map mode controls. It returns nothing.

label: Clear struggle highlight
summary: Removes the highlight from a struggle's border on the map.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it when the mouse leaves a HUD element. It returns nothing.

label: Clear host error
summary: Clears the multiplayer host error.
details: Vanilla calls it on a click in the multiplayer screen. It returns nothing.

label: Clear observer
summary: Stops observing, going by its name.
details: Vanilla calls it on click in the HUD. It returns nothing; the game documents nothing more.

label: Clear tutorial popup reset
summary: Going by its name, clears a reset state of the reactive tutorial popups.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Close all tooltips
summary: Closes every open tooltip.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla calls it on click in the tooltip definitions. It returns nothing.

label: Close game view
summary: Closes the game view with the given name.
details: Vanilla calls it with names such as 'outliner' and 'lobby_helper_window' when the multiplayer lobby finishes. It returns nothing.

fields.name: view
fields.text: The name of the view to close.

label: Join if both filled
summary: Joins two texts, but only when neither is empty.
details: Going by its name and use: vanilla joins an icon and a space, so nothing is added when there is no icon. It returns text.

fields.name: first
fields.text: The first text.

fields.name: second
fields.text: The second text.

label: Join texts
summary: Joins two texts into one.
details: Vanilla uses it in decision texts, for example to put "Currently Equipped:" in front of a name. It returns text.

fields.name: first
fields.text: The first text.

fields.name: second
fields.text: The second text.

label: Game concept link
summary: Going by its name and use, writes a game concept key as text with the words you choose.
details: Vanilla passes a concept key and a display text, for example `Concept('court_amenities','Servants')`, often followed by `|E` which marks a concept link. It returns text.

fields.name: concept
fields.text: The key of the game concept.

fields.name: text
